"Realistically home security is practical. Bike theft rings are HUGE here, so security can be a deterrent. I'm not against protecting your home.  But, Analyzing this situation has helped me deal with some of the fear this random sales guy tried to introduce. Damn he pissed me off."

"Honestly the only point he made that was particularly useful was having to prove to police or insurance that something happened.  There are many ways to keep your home safe. Meet your neighbors, keep a light on a timer, get a motion sensor light. Etc."

"I keep coming back to it. But that tapping into fear to sell a product really pisses me off. Manipulation of people through fear is the root of a lot of our systemic issues. Many people justify their shitty/racist opinions because someone taught them to fear something."
"It could be a family member, the news media, movies, religion. Whatever. As soon as someone teaches you to fear something, they hold power over you and can use that fear to their own advantage."

"He tried to get us to confirm that we'd sign up but I jumped in with "we'll call when we're ready" got his full name and we ended that whole thing.  It was the most predatory sales experience I've had in a while. The tapping into fear really pissed me off."

"So my partner and I have had enough of this at this point. My partner pulls the best power move "I'm working, I need to be in a meeting, wrap this up."  We get the "oh I'm a manager so I can give you a better deal, bs" but I'm pretty sure he could tell we weren't biting."

"Then we take a step back. He says "There are two times when a homeowner typically signs up with us: when they first buy a home and... Well you can guess the second."  Here he's trying to convince us that we would be smarter to sign up early. (Remember all that fear he taught us?)"

"This part is really insidious. He's trying to teach us how to be afraid. He's introducing us to being afraid for our property. Being afraid someone might take our things. This is important for a security company, because if we aren't afraid we won't buy their products."

"So at this point my partner and I are just starting at him. We have 7 degrees between the two of us. We smell bullshit. So this ballsy sales guy launches the next tactic, Fear. He goes into detail about how thieves target new homeowners, how they find our house, how they get in."

"First he started with "Did they tell you I would be stopping by?" Of course we say "No." B/c this is a private company that really has no part in the buying process. That kind of tactic is meant to make the customer feel bad, like their agents potentially withheld or forgot info."

"Then he starts asking if we know what we're doing. Have we considered security? We're young new homeowners so we might not know we're supposed to! Remember he's 'the expert' here. This part is supposed to make us feel incompetent. But don't worry "the expert" can guide us."

"Next he launched into how old and trusted this company is. "Generations within families recommend us!" And he's asking info about us to show he cares about us as people (and probably gathering data, too). In this part he's the expert who cares. We should just trust what he says."

"Geeeeeeze just had a certain security company (that sends a million mailers) hit up our house for the first time.  That sales guy had a talk that would probably work on some people. But it was riddled with shitty tactics. And GOODNESS was he entitled sounding. Let's analyze it."
